data.one_liner: Generates strongly-typed Dart classes for Flutter assets, fonts, and colors to avoid string-based APIs.
data.what_it_does: It reads your pubspec.yaml configuration and asset folders to generate safe, static reference classes. This eliminates string typos when loading images, fonts, or colors in your widgets.
use_when: You want type safety for asset paths, fonts, and colors in your Flutter app.
You want to avoid runtime errors from typos in string-based asset paths.
avoid_when: Your project does not use local assets, custom fonts, or generated color files.
You prefer completely manual string references for resources.
strengths: Eliminates string-based asset paths and potential typos.
Integrates seamlessly with build_runner and pubspec.yaml configurations.
Supports specialized integrations like flutter_svg, rive, and lottie.
weaknesses: Requires running a code generator whenever assets are added or modified.
Adds build-time overhead to your project development workflow.
data.setup_notes: Add flutter_gen_runner to your dev_dependencies and build_runner to your pubspec.yaml, then configure flutter_gen and run build_runner.
